Retrieval System Design Notes

This report walks through the design of the ingestion and retrieval pipeline built for the document search project. It covers the loading stage, the cleaning stage, and the chunking stage, and explains the reasoning behind each choice. The goal throughout has been to keep every stage simple, inspectable, and free of hidden network dependencies so the whole pipeline can run offline during development and testing.

Fixed-size chunking remains useful as a fallback for the minority of documents that have little or no paragraph structure to lean on, or as a safety net inside the paragraph strategy itself when an individual paragraph turns out to be unusually long.

Quarterly Retrieval Report

Section 1: Overview
The pipeline ingests documents and normalizes them before indexing.
Users don’t need to reformat anything by hand; the loader handles it.

Section 2: Cleaning Rules
Cleaning removes noise while keeping numbers like 42 and 3.14 intact.
Headings such as Section 2 must survive cleaning unchanged.

Section 3: Summary
This closes the report with a final note about owners’ responsibilities.

Quarterly retrieval pipeline notes.

The intake step normalizes every document to plain text before anything
gets embedded or indexed. This keeps the downstream chunking logic simple
because it never has to know whether a document originally came from a
PDF, a web page, or a markdown file.

document loader end-to-end.
